title: Zero Verschiebung forces generation by primitive functions
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] of characteristic $p>0$, and let $G$ be a commutative affine $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $C=k[G]$ with comultiplication $\Delta$ and counit $\epsilon$ [lem-sfb-affine-group-coordinate-hopf]. Let $G^{(p)}$, $C^{(p)}$ and $V_G:G^{(p)}\to G$ be the Frobenius twist and the canonical Verschiebung constructed in [lem-sfb-affine-group-frobenius-verschiebung]. Let $u^{(p)}:k\to C^{(p)}$ be the structure map. If $V_G$ is the zero group homomorphism, meaning $V_G^*=u^{(p)}\epsilon:C\to C^{(p)}$, then $C$ is generated as a $k$-algebra by its primitive elements: every $c\in C$ is a polynomial with coefficients in $k$ in finitely many elements $x$ satisfying $\Delta(x)=x\otimes1+1\otimes x$. Neither smoothness nor connectedness of $G$, nor perfection of $k$, is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 14.48, printed pp.295-296, together with the equivalent coordinate-algebra characterization in Definition 14.45, printed p.295. This is the primitive-generation consequence of the Verschiebung criterion, for arbitrary commutative affine algebraic groups.

proof.text: For any extension $K/k$, put $C_K=K\otimes_k C$ and $P(C)=\ker d$, where $d(c)=\Delta(c)-c\otimes1-1\otimes c$. The scalar extension of the coordinate Hopf maps gives the maps for $G_K$. Choose a $k$-basis of $K$. Write an element of $C_K$ uniquely as a finite sum $\sum_i\lambda_i\otimes c_i$ with distinct basis elements $\lambda_i$. Its reduced coproduct is $\sum_i\lambda_i\otimes d(c_i)$ in $K\otimes_k(C\otimes_k C)$, so it vanishes exactly when every $c_i\in P(C)$. Thus $P(C_K)=K\otimes_kP(C)$. This argument does not require finite-dimensional $C$. We will prove generation over an algebraic closure $K$ and descend using this equality in the last step.

source.place: 14.48, p.296, opening field-extension reduction; kernel comparison written out

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $K/k$. By Verschiebung base change, $V_{G_K}=0$. If $D_K(M)\hookrightarrow G_K$ is any diagonalizable closed subgroup, naturality gives $V_{D_K(M)}=0$. The diagonalizable clause makes this map an isomorphism. A zero isomorphism forces the group to be trivial: on every algebra-valued point its identity map is the constant identity-element map. Hence $G_K$ has no nontrivial diagonalizable closed subgroup. In the following steps all groups and maps are over $K$.

Apply the additive-filtration theorem to $G_K$, obtaining $1=G_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq G_s=G_K$ with exact sequences $0\to G_{j-1}\to G_j\xrightarrow{q_j}Q_j\to0$ and closed embeddings $\iota_j:Q_j\hookrightarrow\mathbf G_a$. Every $G_j$ has zero Verschiebung by the closed-subgroup clause. We prove by induction on $j$ that $G_j$ has a closed embedding into a finite power of $\mathbf G_a$. For $j=0$, use the identity of the trivial group with $\mathbf G_a^0$. Fix $j\geq1$ and assume a closed embedding $z:N=G_{j-1}\hookrightarrow\mathbf G_a^r$ has been constructed. Put $B=G_j$, $Q=Q_j$, $q=q_j$.

source.place: 14.48, p.296, induction on a subnormal series; 14.21, pp.284-285

proof.text: For each coordinate homomorphism $\varphi:N\to\mathbf G_a$ of $z$, apply the affine pushout theorem to form $E=(B\times\mathbf G_a)/\{(n,-\varphi(n))\}$, with exact row $0\to\mathbf G_a\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{q'}Q\to0$ and $b:B\to E$ satisfying $bi=j\varphi$. Both $B$ and $\mathbf G_a$ have zero Verschiebung, the latter by the Witt calculation. The product and quotient clauses therefore give $V_E=0$, since $B\times\mathbf G_a\to E$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented. This construction uses no surjectivity of $B(R)\to Q(R)$ before an fppf covering.

source.place: 14.48, p.296, pushout square and vanishing of V on its lower middle term

proof.text: The field $K$ is perfect, $Q$ is a closed subgroup of $\mathbf G_a$, and the pushout row is a commutative affine finite-type extension by $\mathbf G_a$. The Witt-pullback theorem supplies $h:Q\to\mathbf G_a$ and $a:E\to W_{2,K}$ with $\tau a=hq'$ and identifies $E$ with the pullback extension. Naturality gives $V_{W_2}a^{(p)}=aV_E=0$. By the explicit formula $V_{W_2}(x_0,x_1)=(0,x_0)$, the first-coordinate morphism of $a^{(p)}$ is zero. Equivalently $(\tau a)^{(p)}=(hq')^{(p)}=0$, using the canonical twists of $W_2$ and $\mathbf G_a$ over $\mathbf F_p$. Over perfect $K$ the Frobenius automorphism is invertible, so twisting has an inverse scalar-transport functor and detects equality of morphisms. Consequently $hq'=0$. Since $q'$ is an epimorphism of fppf sheaves, $h=0$. This is an equality of twisted morphisms, not merely a statement about their geometric points or the $p$-th powers of their coordinate functions.

For $h=0$, the pullback is $Q\times\ker\tau=Q\times\mathbf G_a$. Transport its second projection to a homomorphism $r_E:E\to\mathbf G_a$ with $r_Ej=1$. Then $\widetilde\varphi=r_Eb:B\to\mathbf G_a$ extends $\varphi$, since $\widetilde\varphi i=r_Ej\varphi=\varphi$. Do this for the $r$ coordinates of $z$ and let $\widetilde z:B\to\mathbf G_a^r$ be their product. Its restriction to $N$ is exactly $z$. The empty family when $r=0$ gives the unique map to the trivial group.

source.place: 14.48, p.296, splitting the pushout gives extension of each coordinate homomorphism

proof.text: Define $u=(\widetilde z,\iota_jq):B\to\mathbf G_a^{r+1}$. Its scheme-theoretic kernel is trivial: on every commutative $K$-algebra $R$, an element in the kernel lies in $N(R)$ because $\iota_j$ is a closed embedding and $\ker q=N$; on $N(R)$ its first coordinates are $z_R$, whose kernel is trivial. These functorial identities identify the kernel scheme with the trivial group. Apply the homomorphism-factorization theorem to $u$. All groups are affine, hence separated, and of finite type. The quotient factor represents the fppf sheaf $B/1=B$, so it is an isomorphism; the other factor is a closed immersion. Thus $u$ is the required closed embedding. This proves the induction step and yields a closed embedding $G_K\hookrightarrow\mathbf G_a^n$ for some finite $n$.

The pullback on coordinate rings of this closed embedding is a surjection $K[T_1,\ldots,T_n]\to C_K$, by the affine closed-immersion criterion. Let $x_i$ be the image of $T_i$. The coordinate coproduct of the additive group sends $T_i$ to $T_i\otimes1+1\otimes T_i$; preservation of multiplication of group schemes gives $\Delta(x_i)=x_i\otimes1+1\otimes x_i$. Thus $C_K$ is generated by finitely many primitives. For $n=0$ the same surjection says that $C_K=K$.

Let $A\subseteq C$ be the $k$-subalgebra generated by $P(C)$. Step 1 shows that every primitive of $C_K$ is a finite $K$-linear combination of elements of $P(C)$, so the generation just proved says the image of $K\otimes_k A\to K\otimes_k C$ is all of $C_K$. For $c\in C$, express $1\otimes c$ as $\sum_{i=1}^t\alpha_i\otimes a_i$ with $a_i\in A$. Choose a $k$-linear map $\ell:K\to k$ with $\ell(1)=1$, by completing $1$ to a $k$-basis of $K$. Applying $\ell\otimes1_C$ gives $c=\sum_i\ell(\alpha_i)a_i\in A$. Hence $A=C$, with exactly the claimed finite-polynomial meaning of generation. No smoothness or connectedness has entered, and the original $k$ need not be perfect.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q12-741cf2ecd (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all nine steps, all five new statement-only nodes, every cited statement, and Milne iAG2017 at Def 14.45/Prop 14.48 (pp.295-296), 11.39-11.44 (pp.224-227), 15.25-15.27 (pp.315-316), 14.21 (pp.284-285) and 16.13(a) (p.328). This is a first delivery: there is no repair note, the item is still unsplit on live and side-live, and its statement and stmt_deps are byte-identical. The delivered nodes contain no SGA citation and no doubled backslashes. The proof follows 14.48 exactly. Step 1 descends primitives through a basis expansion. Step 2 rules out diagonalizable subgroups: V vanishes on them and is also an isomorphism, so they are trivial. Steps 3-4 set up an explicit induction over the 16.13(a)+14.21 filtration and form the antidiagonal pushout, with V_E=0 from the product and quotient clauses. Step 5 uses 15.27 over the perfect field K: V_{W2}a^(p)=aV_E=0 with V_{W2}(x0,x1)=(0,x0) gives (hq')^(p)=0, inverting the twist along Frobenius gives hq'=0, and h=0 because q' is an epimorphism. This is valid without reducedness. Step 6 builds the retraction; step 7 shows the kernel is trivial on all R-points and applies the factorization node; steps 8-9 give primitive generators and descend them with a k-linear l, l(1)=1. New-node tests: c_p equals Milne's f1, the W2 law is associative, and VF(a,b)=(0,a^p)=p(a,b). The perfect-field hypothesis on the 15.27 node is needed, since a·f1 is a pullback only for a p-th power a. The filtration node was checked on Z/p, alpha_p^r, Ga and the trivial group, and it excludes mu_p. None of the new nodes duplicates an existing node or restates the item: perfect-unipotent-additive-series and unipotent-central-additive-subgroup assume smooth and connected, Verschiebung naturality is new, and the pushout node only specialises affine-normal-quotient-geometry. Batch-5: lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homomorphism-factorization reaches lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change, a Mathlib leaf saying fppf coverings are stable under base change. That is a generic site axiom, not part of the trace-formula or Poincaré-duality statements or their proofs, so I accept the citation. The declared tool_uses (closed-immersion affine-cover criterion, tensor pushout) are generic Mathlib leaves, and I accept them.
